explanation: A semibreve (whole note) lasts twice as long as a minim (half note). The names are medieval: breve meant short and minim smallest, before notes came to be held longer over the centuries.

claims.text: A semibreve (whole note) lasts four crotchet beats.
A minim (half note) lasts two crotchet beats.
'Breve' comes from the Latin brevis, short, and 'minim' from minima, smallest.
In medieval notation the breve was a short value and the minim was introduced as the smallest; over the centuries the same note shapes came to be held much longer.

issues.note: The labels use only the British names (semibreve, minim). Players taught whole note and half note, mainly in the US and part of Canada, get no foothold and face a coin flip, while the names also pull the wrong way for guessers (minim sounds short). CONTENT_GUIDE 3.3 asks for both names where usage differs. Fix: label the sides 'A semibreve (whole note)' and 'A minim (half note)', or cut the item. The explanation already gives the American names.

editor.reason: A pass, B revise. B's regional issue is real (§3.3, selfCheck regional): the labels give only the British names, so a player taught whole note and half note has no foothold. Adding the American names would also remove the counterintuitive trap the item is built on, so the redraft needs a different design. Every claim is also high risk on knowledge only. Cut.
